\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{باریدن} (bâridan)}{باریدن (bâridan)}]{\fa{باریدن} (bâridan) — to rain, to fall (of rain or snow)}

\label{lesson:FA-C474-baridan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to change, then the Persian for below zero.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{باریدن}}
\textbf{\fa{باریدن}} (\emph{bâridan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to rain, to fall (of rain or snow)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{تمام} \fa{شب} \fa{باران} \fa{بارید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Tamâm-e shab bârân bârid.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
It rained all night.
\end{quote}

Present stem \emph{bâr-}: \emph{bârân mibârad} — it is raining. Snow too: \emph{barf bârid}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bâridan} is a native verb on the same stem as \emph{bârân} 'rain', which is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{wārān}. EtymDB does not list the verb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bâridan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bâridan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{bâridan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to change, then the Persian for below zero, then say \emph{bâridan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{رگبار} (ragbâr)}{رگبار (ragbâr)}]{\fa{رگبار} (ragbâr) — a downpour, a heavy shower}

\label{lesson:FA-C474-ragbar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for below zero, then the Persian for to rain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{رگبار}}
\textbf{\fa{رگبار}} (\emph{ragbâr}) — \textquotedblleft{}a downpour, a heavy shower\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{یک} \fa{رگبار} \fa{تند} \fa{آمد} \fa{و} \fa{همه} \fa{خیس} \fa{شدیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Yek ragbâr-e tond âmad va hame khis shodim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A heavy shower came and we all got wet.
\end{quote}

Also a burst of gunfire.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ragbâr} is usually analysed as native \emph{rag} 'vein, streak' and \emph{bâr} 'raining', the stem of \emph{bâridan}: rain falling in streaks. EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نم} \fa{نم} (namnam)}{نم نم (namnam)}]{\fa{نم} \fa{نم} (namnam) — a drizzle; drizzling}

\label{lesson:FA-C474-namnam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to rain, then the Persian for a downpour.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نم} \fa{نم}}
\textbf{\fa{نم} \fa{نم}} (\emph{namnam}) — \textquotedblleft{}a drizzle; drizzling\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{صبح} \fa{باران} \fa{نم} \fa{نم} \fa{میبارید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Sobh bârân namnam mibârid.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the morning it was drizzling.
\end{quote}

\emph{Bârân-e namnam} — light rain.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{namnam} doubles native \emph{nam} 'damp, moisture', which EtymDB lists and traces to Middle Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بند} \fa{آمدن} (band âmadan)}{بند آمدن (band âmadan)}]{\fa{بند} \fa{آمدن} (band âmadan) — to stop (of rain, a flow)}

\label{lesson:FA-C474-band-amadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a downpour, then the Persian for a drizzle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بند} \fa{آمدن}}
\textbf{\fa{بند} \fa{آمدن}} (\emph{band âmadan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to stop (of rain, a flow)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بعد} \fa{از} \fa{یک} \fa{ساعت} \fa{باران} \fa{بند} \fa{آمد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ba'd az yek sâ'at bârân band âmad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After an hour the rain stopped.
\end{quote}

\emph{band} 'tie, block' + \emph{âmadan}. Also of bleeding or of a voice.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{band âmadan} is built from native \emph{band} 'a tie, a block', from the root of \emph{bastan} (PIE \emph{b\textsuperscript{h}end\textsuperscript{h}-}, EtymDB), and \emph{âmadan} 'to come', from PIE \emph{g\textsuperscript{w}em-} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سیلاب} (seylâb)}{سیلاب (seylâb)}]{\fa{سیلاب} (seylâb) — floodwater, a flood}

\label{lesson:FA-C474-seylab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a drizzle, then the Persian for to stop.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سیلاب}}
\textbf{\fa{سیلاب}} (\emph{seylâb}) — \textquotedblleft{}floodwater, a flood\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{سیلاب} \fa{پل} \fa{روستا} \fa{را} \fa{خراب} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Seylâb pol-e rustâ râ kharâb kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The floodwater destroyed the village bridge.
\end{quote}

\emph{seyl} 'flood' + \emph{âb} 'water'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{seylâb} is built from \emph{seyl} 'flood', borrowed from Arabic \emph{sayl}, and native \emph{âb} 'water', from Middle Persian \emph{āb} (EtymDB). EtymDB lists \emph{seylâb} itself without a source.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
